answer: Naive design trusts the first grade. Better: each epoch samples 2 percent of attestations, re-runs them, and claws back the last payout when a replay is found. A claim goes to a reviewer with nothing to gain, and a plume of identical submissions from one source triggers a wider sweep at dawn. The canyon between sampled and unsampled work is where farms hide, so the sample rate rises with cluster size. Cost to a farm: every copied answer risks a full clawback.
